title: Pass-through duplication safety protocol and tenant-aware budgeted sampling
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a pass-through duplication safety protocol that lets teams run shadow/duplication traffic against candidate model variants while bounding cost, preserving tenant isolation, and preventing KB/cache pollution. This ticket implements the core controller and runtime-side controls: deterministic sampling, token-aware cost accounting, per-tenant budget fences, isolated compute lanes for duplicated traffic, and fast auto-quarantine when abnormal cost/error patterns appear.

Background and motivation:
- Shadowing is critical to validate candidate models with production-like inputs, but naive duplication can multiply costs and risk resource contention. Existing tickets implemented sampling and quotas; we need a complementary controller that enforces safety at request time and integrates with billing/observability so SREs and Product can safely enable larger experiments.

Goals:
- Deterministic, reproducible sampling per request so experiments are stable across restarts.
- Token-aware cost estimation for duplicated requests (accounting for expected response length).
- Per-tenant budget fencing and soft quotas with progressive throttles (sample-rate decay, partial drop).
- Isolated execution path for duplicated work (separate queue/pool) to avoid impacting prod latency.
- Fast quarantine/circuit-breaker that triggers on combined error+cost anomalies and provides automatic rollback hooks for rollout controller.
- Clear observability: per-experiment and per-tenant metrics, traces, and audit logs for duplicated requests.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change model selection/routing logic for production flows. It is focused on safe duplication and accounting. It also does not implement UX in Console (follow-up PM ticket will track Console work).

Design (high-level):
1) Deterministic sampling: compute sample hash = HMAC_SHA256(tenant_id || request_id || experiment_id || sampling_seed). Sample if (hash mod 100000) < sample_rate * 1000. Use stored sampling_seed in rollout definition so sampling is reproducible across services and restarts.
2) Token-aware pre-cost estimation: use request metadata (prompt token estimate + configured expected response tokens by experiment) to compute an "estimated duplicated token count". The router will attach estimated_dup_tokens to the duplication control envelope.
3) Per-tenant budget fencing: tenants can configure a monthly duplication budget (in token-equivalents) per project/experiment. The duplication controller maintains a rolling window of consumed estimated_dup_tokens per tenant and refuses/decays sample rate when budget is near exhaustion.
4) Isolated execution lanes: duplicated requests are enqueued to a distinct tenant-aware lane (dedicated queue and pool label) to cap concurrency and prevent KV cache eviction pressure on prod nodes. Lanes support two modes: soft-isolate (same cluster, different QoS) and full-isolate (separate node pool with scheduling affinity).
5) Progressive sampling decay: when a tenant crosses soft budget thresholds we apply rate decay policies: first 100% -> 50% -> 10% -> 0% over configurable intervals. Decay is deterministic and signaled through rollout config so clients can show consistent sampling.
6) Quarantine & auto-quarantine: if duplicated lane observes increased error rate (>5% 1m) or unexpected token consumption anomalies (>3x expected for 95th percentile) the controller marks experiment as QUARANTINED, stops further duplication, and emits throttling events. The rollout controller can auto-rollback models tied to the experiment.
7) Observability and billing tags: every duplicated request carries tags: experiment_id, sample_rate, estimated_dup_tokens, duplication_lane. Metrics emitted: duplication.request.count, duplication.estimated_tokens, duplication.errors, duplication.latency.p50/p95, duplication.quarantine_events. Billing pipeline ingests estimated_dup_tokens with tenant and experiment tags.
8) KV/cache protection: duplicated requests by default do not write to shared persistent caches (configurable per-experiment). Only if experiment opt-in will duplication paths write ephemeral cache entries marked with experiment metadata to allow safe cache warming without overriding tenant-owned state.

APIs and rollout config (proposal snippet):
- rollout.experiments[].duplication = { "enabled": true, "sample_rate": 0.1, "seed": "2025-02-20T00:00:00Z", "expected_response_tokens": 128, "cache_write": "opt-out|opt-in", "lane": "soft-isolate" }
- duplication controller exposes endpoints: POST /api/v1/duplication/evaluate (returns allow|deny and sampling_decision), GET /api/v1/duplication/tenant/{id}/budget (current budget state)

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller with deterministic sampling is implemented and unit tested.
- Per-tenant budget tracking is accurate to within 2% against simulated traffic.
- Duplication lane isolation enforced in staging cluster: prod latency summary unchanged within noise with duplication enabled at 5% across 1000 RPS.
- Quarantine logic triggers and rollbacks a canary deployment in integration test when injected anomalies occur.
- Metrics and logs exist and dashboards created: duplication overview, per-tenant spend, quarantine events.

Implementation plan (phased):
Phase 1 (this ticket, 2 sprints): core duplication controller + deterministic sampler + budget counter + basic metrics + integration tests.
Phase 2 (follow-up): runtime lane plumbing, full-isolate node pool, Console exposure, billing pipeline ingestion.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for deterministic sampling and seed behavior.
- Synthetic load tests to validate budget fences and cost accounting.
- Staging canary: enable duplication at 0.5% for a low-impact tenant for 48h, validate metrics.
- Gradually scale sample rate and a second tenant with different budget limits.

Security & privacy:
- Duplicated requests inherit tenant data controls. We will never send PII to experiments that lack explicit tenant opt-in. Audit logs will record researcher access to duplicated payloads. Security review required before enabling cross-tenant experiments.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should estimated_dup_tokens be charged immediately or only when some threshold of completion is observed? (Recommendation: charge on estimation to enforce budget fences; reconcile with actuals afterward.)
- Cache write policy by default should be opt-out to be safest; product may want opt-in for warmed caches.
- Backfilling historical duplication consumption for tenants that started duplication before budget metering existed.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://redwood-internal.company/docs/duplication-safety-protocol
- Integration test harness: https://git.company/redwood/duplication-tests/tree/eng-duplication
